wv_entrance_boulders.blurb: Entrance Boulders is the first cluster of blocks a climber meets at Upper Rock City in Coopers Rock State Forest, near Morgantown. It is a pure bouldering zone with a few dozen problems spread over several small boulders and nooks. The grades are friendly: most problems fall between VB-level and V3, a handful reach V4 and V5, and the hardest lines are a minority. Landings are mostly low-key and the problems are short, so it works well as a warm-up before heading deeper into the forest or as a relaxed session for newer boulderers. Because it sits closest to the road end, expect other visitors and walkers passing through.

wv_southern_pillar_west_side.blurb: The west face of the Southern Pillar at Seneca Rocks, in Pendleton County within Monongahela National Forest, holds a couple dozen multi-pitch and single-pitch lines on quartzite. Nearly all of it is traditional climbing, with just a pair of bolted lines. Grades span roughly 5.5 to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.7 to 5.11 range, so it suits parties comfortable with old-school ratings and gear placement. Many routes finish at bolted anchors, and the rappel descent drops into the chimney system. It is one of the shorter walks at Seneca and tends to stay cool, which makes it a reasonable pick on warm days.
wv_southern_pillar_west_side.approach: Walk up Roy Gap Road from the Seneca Rocks visitor area. Where the road bends at a small turnaround near the large culvert, a trail leaves on the right and leads to the base of the pillar. It is the shortest approach at Seneca.

wv_big_blocks.blurb: Big Blocks is a set of large boulders in the Roadside zone of Coopers Rock State Forest, just past the Sunset Wall cliff. The blocks are mostly used for top-roping, with a few leadable lines and some boulder problems on the side facing the river. Difficulty spans a wide range: easy low-fifth-class climbs and a simple scramble up the block, through the middle 5.x grades, to a few 5.11 and 5.12 lines, while the boulder problems run from VB or V0 up to about V4. The side facing the cliff stays shady. Setting up top-ropes means rigging off trees, so bring extra webbing. A short walk from the lot keeps it popular with beginners and families.
wv_big_blocks.approach: From the main lot, follow the trail past the climbers kiosk and the roadside boulders. A few minutes along, Sunset Wall appears on the left, and the Big Blocks stand just beyond it on the right.

wv_ninja_wall.blurb: Ninja Wall is the east-facing section of the Guide Wall cliff in Smoke Hole Canyon, in the eastern part of the state. It is a bolted face with a small number of trad lines mixed in, around two dozen sport routes in all. Grades start near 5.5 and climb to the 5.12 range, though the middle is thickest: lots of 5.10s plus a good selection of 5.7 to 5.9 lines. Because the wall catches plenty of shade, it is regarded as a comfortable summer option compared with its sunnier neighbor. Expect canyon-style limestone climbing with a moderate hike to reach the cliff base.
wv_ninja_wall.approach: Walk the trail up to the base of the Guide Wall cliff line, then continue along the base toward climber's right to reach Ninja Wall. It shares its approach with the neighboring Sunshine Wall.

wv_cotton_top_2.blurb: Cotton Top sits on Cotton Hill, one of the farthest-downstream crags in the New River Gorge, below the Hawks Nest dam. The hillside is mostly a sport crag with a scattering of trad lines and some boulder problems. Roped grades run from about 5.7 up to the low 5.13s, but the weight of the area is in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it is better suited to climbers past the beginner stage. The bouldering ranges from easy to hard. Expect a short, steep uphill walk, and note that the vertical wall tends to hold water for a day or two after heavy rain.

wv_pirate_s_cove.blurb: Pirate's Cove is a waterfall-fed, overhanging cove on the shore of Summersville Lake in the New River Gorge region. It is a mixed bag: about half the problems are bouldering, with a good number of trad lines and a few sport routes. Boulder grades run from VB to V8, while the roped climbs cluster around 5.10 to 5.11 with a couple harder ones reaching 5.13. The cove is a cold-weather destination, since the lake covers the base when the water is high and the lines are only reachable when the level is lowered. The walk-in is longer than at neighboring walls, and in summer some visitors arrive by boat.

wv_the_prize_sector.blurb: This bouldering sector lies beside the Cheat River in the Cheat Canyon Wildlife Management Area, downstream of the first sector. It holds around 27 sandstone problems on isolated, water-polished boulders. The spread is wide: a single easy line, then a cluster of V2 to V4 problems, a handful in the V5 to V8 range, and a run of hard projects at V10 and above. The stone is fine-grained and kind to skin, and slopers dominate. Boulders are exposed to plenty of sun and dry quickly, so it is a good warm-season choice. River level matters for the lowest blocks, and it is a quiet spot with a pretty setting.
